questions.stem: The classical complement pathway shown begins when C1 binds antibody. Which region of the antibody does C1q actually attach to?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Free mannose residues on the antibody

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Fc region of antigen-bound IgM or IgG

choices.label: D
choices.text: The J chain of secretory IgA

explanation.summary: C1q binds the Fc portions of antibody (IgM or IgG) that is already bound to antigen, activating C1r/C1s to cleave C4 and C2 and assemble the classical C3 convertase (C4b2b).
explanation.whyCorrect: C1q binds the Fc portions of antibody (IgM or IgG) that is already bound to antigen, activating C1r/C1s to cleave C4 and C2 and assemble the classical C3 convertase (C4b2b).

questions.stem: This patient has recurrent episodes of non-pitting facial and lip swelling (angioedema) without urticaria or itching. Deficiency of which regulatory protein classically causes this?

explanation.summary: Hereditary angioedema results from C1-inhibitor deficiency, leading to unchecked bradykinin generation and episodic angioedema without urticaria. Because it is bradykinin-mediated (not histamine-mediated), antihistamines are ineffective and ACE inhibitors can precipitate attacks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hereditary angioedema results from C1-inhibitor deficiency, leading to unchecked bradykinin generation and episodic angioedema without urticaria. Because it is bradykinin-mediated (not histamine-mediated), antihistamines are ineffective and ACE inhibitors can precipitate attacks.

questions.stem: The middle panel shows the membrane attack complex lysing a microbe. Deficiency of the terminal components that form this complex (C5-C9) predisposes to infection with which organism?

explanation.summary: The membrane attack complex (C5b-9) is critical for lysing Neisseria, so terminal-complement (C5-C9) deficiencies cause recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal/gonococcal) infections. Other panels show C3b opsonization and C3a/C5a leukocyte recruitment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The membrane attack complex (C5b-9) is critical for lysing Neisseria, so terminal-complement (C5-C9) deficiencies cause recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal/gonococcal) infections. Other panels show C3b opsonization and C3a/C5a leukocyte recruitment.

questions.stem: Red cells shuttle C3b-tagged immune complexes to phagocytes via CR1, as shown. Deficiency of early classical complement components (C1q, C4, C2) impairs this clearance and predisposes to which autoimmune disease?

explanation.summary: Early classical-pathway components opsonize immune complexes with C3b for erythrocyte CR1-mediated transport to the liver and spleen. Their deficiency leads to immune-complex accumulation and is strongly associated with SLE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early classical-pathway components opsonize immune complexes with C3b for erythrocyte CR1-mediated transport to the liver and spleen. Their deficiency leads to immune-complex accumulation and is strongly associated with SLE.

questions.stem: In the lectin pathway shown, mannose-binding lectin uses MASP-2 to cleave C4 and C2. MASP-2 is functionally analogous to which component of the classical pathway?

explanation.summary: The lectin pathway mirrors the classical pathway: MBL replaces C1q, and MASP-2 performs the C4/C2-cleaving protease role of C1r/C1s, generating the same C3 convertase (C4b2b) without requiring antibody.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lectin pathway mirrors the classical pathway: MBL replaces C1q, and MASP-2 performs the C4/C2-cleaving protease role of C1r/C1s, generating the same C3 convertase (C4b2b) without requiring antibody.

questions.stem: Unlike the other complement pathways, the alternative pathway shown does not require antibody or lectin binding. How is it initiated on a microbial surface?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spontaneous low-level hydrolysis of C3 ('C3 tickover')

explanation.summary: C3 continuously undergoes spontaneous hydrolysis ('tickover'). C3b deposited on a foreign surface binds factor B, which factor D cleaves to form C3bBb, stabilized by properdin. Host surfaces are protected by regulatory proteins.
explanation.whyCorrect: C3 continuously undergoes spontaneous hydrolysis ('tickover'). C3b deposited on a foreign surface binds factor B, which factor D cleaves to form C3bBb, stabilized by properdin. Host surfaces are protected by regulatory proteins.

questions.stem: All three complement pathways in this schematic converge on C3 convertase and then a shared terminal pathway (C5-C9). What lytic structure does this terminal pathway assemble?

explanation.summary: After C5 is cleaved, C5b recruits C6, C7, C8, and multiple C9 molecules to form the membrane attack complex (C5b-9), a pore that osmotically lyses the target cell. This is the shared terminal step of all three pathways.
explanation.whyCorrect: After C5 is cleaved, C5b recruits C6, C7, C8, and multiple C9 molecules to form the membrane attack complex (C5b-9), a pore that osmotically lyses the target cell. This is the shared terminal step of all three pathways.
